learning_outcomes.text: That students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences;

Promote the development of personality in all its dimensions: scientific, cultural, human, etc.; in such a way that it is reflected in a greater development of critical capacity and a knowledge of problems, leading to an exercise of freedom that, respecting legitimate pluralism, is sensitive to expressions of solidarity and fraternity and helps build spaces of equality, coexistence and friendship.
Understand that it is characteristic of the university spirit to approach the study of one's own discipline critically and reflectively in its connection with other areas of knowledge.
Identify the most relevant questions of human existence present in great religious, humanistic, and scientific creations and adopt a reasoned personal stance towards them.
Discover and judge the anthropological assumptions and ethical repercussions of one's own discipline.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the subject. Training objectives. Work methodology. Activities and class work. Assessment
Email: professional use, best practices, privacy, confidentiality, legal validity, situations to avoid. Professional mail/private mail.
Agenda: personal and collective scheduling of complex tasks over time. Tools available. Follow-up
Meetings: calls, agenda, notification to participants, prior preparation, punctuality, attitude and proactivity of participants, conclusions and minutes, approval of the minutes by participants.
Written technical reports: format, indexes, references, writing style, content organization, basic structure, legal and contractual validity, etc., specific IT tools.
Oral presentations: preparation, time management, interaction with the audience, basic techniques for public speaking, correct use of technical support resources (PPT presentations, videos, etc.)
PowerPoint Presentations: essential concepts for effective presentations.
Excel: essential tool for agile data management in engineering, in written documents and in presentations
Methodologies for effective work in engineering
Several sessions with presentations of engineering projects/works.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a group project and its oral presentation account for 6 points (4.5 for the work, 1.5 for the presentation) out of a total of 10, and in-class questionnaires account for 4 points. For the extraordinary call, an individual project with an oral presentation is evaluated over 6 points, while the grades from the in-class questionnaires (4 points) are retained. Any attempt at fraud, copying, plagiarism, or other irregular behavior is considered a serious infraction.
